fields.description:
## What this ticket is now (rewritten 2026-08-19 after a code-level review)

The original framing of this ticket was WRONG and has been replaced. It claimed ten
model-emitted free-text `criteria` aliases were silently bypassing per-criterion routing, and
proposed constraining the reviewer prompt/schema to the registry vocabulary. A read of the actual
code-review pipeline showed that the premise does not hold and that the proposed remedy would
BREAK a working extensibility mechanism.

### Why the original framing was wrong

1. **`criteria` holds DIMENSION ids, and the vocabulary is open BY DESIGN.**
   `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-base.md:34` instructs the base reviewer:
   "`criteria`: the code-review dimension id(s) the finding maps to (**e.g.** `correctness`,
   `edge-cases`, `error-handling`, `maintainability`, `regression`)". That is an open "e.g." list,
   not a closed enum. The pydantic contract agrees — `CodeFinding.criteria: list[str]`, described
   as "Code-review dimension/overlay id(s) the finding maps to"
   (`src/rebar/llm/code_review/contracts.py`).

2. **Project-supplied criteria are a first-class feature, and the analysis missed them.**
   `src/rebar/llm/code_review/registry.py` exposes a THREE-layer vocabulary:
   `routing_index()` (packaged built-ins only), `effective_routing(repo_root)` (packaged MERGED
   with the project's `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` `code_review` map), and
   `effective_criteria(repo_root)` — "the packaged built-ins union the project ids the overlay
   activates (minus any disabled built-in)". Any check of whether a label is known MUST use the
   effective vocabulary, not the packaged index.

3. **A fixed enum would break the system.** Constraining the schema to a static list would make
   project-supplied criteria unexpressible and would also forbid the base reviewer's designed
   open dimension vocabulary. This is explicitly NOT to be built.

4. **The 0.95 default is intentional, not an accident.** `registry.py` documents
   `DEFAULT_BLOCK_THRESHOLD = 0.95` as "the kernel's default when a criterion has no routing
   entry ... the high-threshold, mostly-advisory v1 stance". Dimensions landing on it is the
   designed posture.

### Measured reality (code-v3 corpus, 1663 sidecars, 5669 label instances)

Of the labels not present in the PACKAGED routing index, the overwhelming majority are correct:
`maintainability` (869), `correctness` (808), `edge-cases` (553) are prompt-specified dimensions;
`bugfix-size-attestation` (61) is a real criterion defined at
`src/rebar/llm/code_review/bugfix_size_gate.py:45` (`CRITERION_ID`);
`project.review-phase-boundaries` (10) is a real PROJECT criterion declared in this repo's
`.rebar/criteria_routing.json` and activated for `code_review`. Only `sec` (8) and
`documentation` (5) are genuine synonym sloppiness.

## Scope — two items

### Item 1 (APPROVED): normalize the two genuine synonyms
`sec` and `documentation` are true synonyms of the packaged criteria `security` and `docs`.
Because they do not match a known criterion id they fall to the default posture instead of their
criterion's tuned threshold.

Normalize them onto their canonical ids. The normalization MUST be a synonym MAPPING, not a
whitelist: a label that matches no known id must pass through UNCHANGED, so that open dimensions
and project criteria are unaffected. Membership must be tested against the EFFECTIVE vocabulary
(`effective_criteria(repo_root)` / `effective_routing(repo_root)`), never the packaged index.

### Item 2 (POSTPONED — do not implement here)
Whether `correctness` / `maintainability` / `edge-cases` should get their own routing entries so
they can be tuned per-dimension is a deliberate POSTURE change with real blast radius: those three
account for ~2230 findings currently sitting on the deliberately-high 0.95 default, so giving them
a normal threshold could materially increase what blocks a change. Operator decision 2026-08-19:
postponed to a future session. Do NOT fold it into this ticket.

### Item 3 (APPROVED): correct the calibration document
`docs/experiments/code-review-threshold-calibration.md` lines 133-140 ("Data-hygiene finding
(discovered work)") records the same mistake this ticket used to make, and will mislead the next
reader. It states the listed labels "are model-emitted free-text aliases that fall through to the
default 0.95 posture and cannot be individually routed" and recommends "The reviewer prompt should
constrain emitted criteria to the registry vocabulary".

Its most concrete error: it lists `project.review-phase-boundaries` as a model-emitted alias. That
is a legitimate project-supplied criterion, and calling it model noise misrepresents the overlay
feature.

Rewrite that section to state: the comparison was made against the PACKAGED routing index rather
than the EFFECTIVE vocabulary; dimension labels are open by design per code-review-base.md; the
0.95 default is the intended v1 posture rather than a bypass; and constraining the prompt to a
fixed vocabulary is explicitly rejected because it would break project criteria. Preserve the one
finding that survives — `sec` and `documentation` are genuine synonyms worth normalizing. Do not
delete the section; a corrected record is more useful than a removed one.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `sec` normalizes to `security` and `documentation` to `docs` before routing/threshold lookup.
- [ ] A label matching no known id passes through UNCHANGED — proven by a test using a project
      criterion and an arbitrary open dimension, neither of which may be dropped or rewritten.
- [ ] Known-id membership is resolved through the EFFECTIVE vocabulary (project overlay included),
      not the packaged index; a test with an overlay-activated project criterion proves it.
- [ ] No fixed enum / closed schema constraint on `criteria` is introduced anywhere.
- [ ] `docs/experiments/code-review-threshold-calibration.md`'s "Data-hygiene finding" section is
      corrected per Item 3, including removing the claim that `project.review-phase-boundaries` is
      model-emitted, and no longer recommends constraining the prompt to the registry vocabulary.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass; existing code-review tests pass unmodified.
fields.title: Normalize the two genuine criteria synonyms (sec/documentation) and correct the calibration doc's data-hygiene finding
